content.thinking:
I need to be careful writing this postmortem — I shouldn't restate the cost figures as if I calculated them myself, and I shouldn't invent my own numbers either. Best to reference what actually happened without presenting given figures as my own computation.

For the root cause: the legacy-checkout-fallback flag was flipped at 08:58, which routed account-page traffic to a spend-summary code path with a pre-existing divide-by-zero defect — no deploy had gone out in the prior week, so this was a latent bug exposed by the flag change rather than a new regression. The incident lasted roughly seven minutes, from onset at 08:58 to recovery at 09:05, which I can state directly since it's a duration figure, not a cost estimate. I'll also flag key assumptions clearly: the flag-to-error correlation rather than proven causality, the impact scope inferred from logs, and the fact that no owner has been identified for the flag change.

assumptions: Mitigation was judged successful because the error rate returned to its prior level within a minute of the flag being reverted; this is a correlation in the metrics, not an independent proof that the flag was the only contributing factor.

Impact is assumed to be confined to the account page / spend-summary path, because every error logged during the window carried the same ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:35. Other endpoints were not separately checked.
The flag change was read from the flag provider's history; who changed it, why, and whether it was intentional were not established during the incident.
The first minute of the incident (08:58) shows the flag evaluating off for only part of traffic, so the switch is assumed to have propagated progressively rather than instantaneously.
The 'latent bad code' alternative was ruled out only by the absence of a deployment in the change log for the week before onset; the change log is assumed to be complete for that period.
The underlying defect is assumed to still be present in production, currently masked by the flag being back on, until the proposed code fix is merged.
input.executive_summary: On 24 September 2026, shoppers trying to load their account page on the online shop began getting errors. The problem started at 08:58 UTC and the service was back to normal by 09:05 UTC — roughly seven minutes. During that window a large minority of account-page requests failed outright; other parts of the shop were not implicated. The cause was a configuration switch that quietly redirected account-page traffic onto a code path containing a long-standing bug; the bug had been in the product for some time but nothing had been sending traffic to it. Our automated responder picked up the alert, identified the switch as the likely trigger, put it back to its previous setting, and confirmed the service had returned to its normal error level before closing out the mitigation. A draft code change to fix the underlying bug has been opened for engineering review. No customer data was affected, and shoppers who retried after 09:05 would have seen the page load normally.
input.root_cause: At 08:58 UTC the feature flag `legacy-checkout-fallback` went from on to off, which moved account-page traffic off the fallback path and onto the non-fallback spend-summary code path, where an unguarded division raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:35. The defect was pre-existing and latent — no deploy or release appears in the change log for the week before onset — so the flag flip, not a code change, is what made it reachable.
